first.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and the single slot must go where the inherited evidence is both load-bearing and weakest against that objective. Activation is the largest deterioration (-6% QoQ) and memory_91 is the most recent, most directly relevant belief, so it is the belief my intended action rests on; but its recorded outcome is week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' — proxy metrics that may not translate into retained, qualified revenue. That makes it consequential and insufficiently supported for this objective, so it is my first pull. My second pull is memory_73: the competitor's entry pricing creates the strongest pull toward promotional_pricing, and that memory is the oldest-but-most-tempting basis for a high-commitment, hard-to-reverse move. Its recorded lift is acquisition and revenue, which is exactly the metric pair that can look strong while importing discount-anchored, churn-prone SMB accounts — a downstream value risk the memory does not appear to have measured. I deliberately did not spend budget on memory_86 or memory_31: onboarding is down only 4%, and while memory_31 carries its own quality risk (cutting required fields can degrade lead qualification and thus qualified revenue even as activation rises), I am not currently intending that action, so verifying it would not change this week's decision. memory_44 is off-path since the pressure is in the SMB segment, and memory_57 targets established customers rather than the falling top-of-funnel. If the archive shows memory_91 measured only engagement with no revenue or retention follow-through, I will treat the activation lift as unproven for this objective and instrument the experiment to read qualified-revenue and retention outcomes rather than engagement alone; if memory_73 shows durable retained revenue rather than a one-time acquisition spike, I will reconsider pricing. Running at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout preserves the option to be wrong.

final.rationale: Both pulls paid off. exp_91 held up better than I feared: activation messaging moved not just the proxy (week-one engagement +11%) but activation itself (+6%) with 30-day retention slightly positive (+1%) rather than negative. That is a lift that does not appear to be borrowed against future churn, which is what the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective requires. It also happens to be sized to the exact wound — activation is down 6% QoQ. exp_73 was the decisive negative result: the 40% discount produced signup +31% and qualified revenue +18%, but 30-day retention -12%, and the source record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy. The acquired cohort does not survive first renewal, so the revenue lift in memory_73 is a timing artifact, not durable revenue. The competitor's entry pricing creates real pressure to match, but matching would import exactly the cohort exp_73 showed we cannot keep — so I am declining the most intuitive response to the most visible threat, on evidence. Committing the slot to activation_messaging at standard experiment scale. Not broad rollout: exp_91's retention signal is only +1% at 30 days, which is thin, and the current -6% activation decline may have a cause the earlier experiment did not face (competitive churn pulling out engaged accounts rather than a genuine activation-mechanism failure). If that is true, activation messaging will underperform its historical result, so I want a read before scaling. I will instrument for 30-day-plus retention and qualified revenue, not engagement alone, so the next agent inherits a durable-value measurement rather than another proxy. Unverified and carried forward as uncertain: memory_86 and memory_31 (onboarding/signup simplification, -4% QoQ). memory_31 in particular claims activation lift from cutting required fields, which is precisely the mechanism that can raise activation while degrading lead qualification and thus qualified revenue — the same proxy-versus-durable-value trap exp_73 exposed. It should be verified before anyone acts on it. memory_57 and memory_44 remain unverified and off-path for the SMB top-of-funnel problem.
